doc: Owner's review decisions on generated Bengali candidates, kept so they can train soft scores later. Ids refer to the sheet of that round (files named in 'file').

motif_round1.rest: owner redraws each by hand on draw_1/draw_2 sheets (pairs.py) as feedback on shape/angle/placement
motif_round1.structural_notes: applied in curate3.py (m001,m002,m005,m010,m021,m023,m024,m030,m034,m037); m018 (owner's 'm015' meant m018). 'm022' in the owner's note meant m021.

principles_from_owner: free (unconnected) stroke ends keep a visible buffer from other strokes
strokes under the purple bar are centred; two strokes share the space under the bar in a balanced way
nothing floats: accents always attach (e.g. to the bar, beside the junction of the body strokes)
strokes that meet share exactly one intersection point (e.g. bottom of a descender)
near-vertical long strokes are exactly vertical; a vertical stroke starts under the bar, not at its far end
owner_preferences: sheet labels should be large and legible (render.py header strip, 0.75 font)
busyness and visual balance are gut-check aesthetics, not hard rules: use as soft taste features only; owner will add concrete reasons when known
hard rule: a stroke that starts below the bar must not wrap round its end and continue above it (engine check no_bar_wrap)

taste_refit_v2.data: round1/2 picks plus owner 1-4 scores on motif pools A and B (soft labels 4=1, 3=.7, 2=.15, 1=0, D ignored)
taste_refit_v2.finding: owner liked 62 of 71 scored letters, so the pools give little contrast: refit weights are near zero and top-30 hit rate (26) equals the base rate; v1 kept as taste_bengali_v1.json
taste_refit_v2.next: need more rejects (harder pools) or topology-aware features to sharpen it
